author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Merrimack Valley defeated Bow 26-6 on Friday night in Penacook, giving the Pride the first 2-0 start in the football program’s history. The result followed an opening victory over Hollis-Brookline and left Bow 0-2 through its first two games.

Holding Bow to one touchdown was central to the win. Merrimack Valley paired that defensive performance with enough scoring to keep the game beyond a one-possession margin, reversing the outcome of last season’s meeting, when Bow won decisively under its new home lights. The early results mark a sharp improvement for a program that entered the new season looking to build consistency.

The 2-0 record will be tested quickly. Merrimack Valley’s next scheduled opponent is St. Thomas Aquinas, followed by games against Kennett, Trinity, Kingswood and Milford. Bow is scheduled to face Kingswood next. September records do not settle a season, but the Pride’s first two games have already established a program milestone and given the team a meaningful platform for the tougher division schedule ahead.
dek: The Pride followed an opening win over Hollis-Brookline by holding Bow to one touchdown in a 26-6 home victory.
headline: Merrimack Valley beats Bow 26-6 for program’s first 2-0 start
